newsitem.title: MEXICO: Desc unit sees output up after JSR deal.
newsitem.headline: Desc unit sees output up after JSR deal.

text.p: Mexico's Industrias Negromex (INSA) plans to raise production of synthetic rubber by 2,000 tonnes if its proposed deal with Japan Synthetic Rubber (JSR) goes ahead, a company official said on Thursday.

He said the agreement was expected to be signed next month, creating a joint venture to produce and market synthetic rubber across the Americas. It was not clear how much rubber INSA currently produces.

On Wednesday, INSA, a unit of industrial holding company Desc's chemical division, said it reached a basic agreement with JSR, and that they planned to open a new factory in Mexico or the United States. It did not give the cost of the deal.
In the initial phase, production by the joint venture would be carried out at INSA's plant in Atlamira, Tamaulipas.
(--Tomas de la Rosa, Mexico City newsroom +525 728-7912)
